headline: Nvidia's share of China's AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026 as Huawei and other Chinese makers gained ground, research firm IDC estimates.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: the IDC figures were read in a full relay of the Reuters report and match the headline; they are one research firm's estimates.
importance_line: What changed is that first-half figures show a US chip maker's lead in China shrinking to about a third of the market as Huawei closes in, which matters first to Chinese AI developers choosing chips, then to governments weighing export controls, then to Nvidia and Huawei, and the doubt is that the numbers are IDC's estimates and that Nvidia has said its own outlook already counts no China data-centre revenue.
summary: Reuters reports that IDC, a market research firm, estimates Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators (the chips that train and run AI models) to China from January to June 2026, down 44% on a year earlier, which gives it a 34% share of the data-centre AI chip market, while Huawei shipped 572,000 for a 28% share. Other Chinese makers are growing too, led by Alibaba's T-Head at 7%, and Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has criticised the US export curbs, saying they forced a US company to hand China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei; Nvidia did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.
notes: Investing.com page (Reuters text) returned HTTP 403; the Reuters report and IDC figures were read in a Yahoo Finance relay. Link kept to the Investing.com copy of Reuters. Nvidia's August-call point is the Yahoo writer's account and is used only in the importance line.
